answers.ask: Where is this set - a house, a school, a park, something stranger?
answers.answer: Set it in a small house, a classic hide-and-seek setting with clear rooms and hiding spots.

answers.ask: How many players per round? Hide-and-seek scales badly: a map sized for 8 is unplayable for 30.
answers.answer: Build it for up to 8 players per round to keep the map compact and playable.
Keep it indoors, using the house interior as the full play space.

scene_prompt: Create a compact indoor hide-and-seek map set entirely inside a small house for up to 8 players. Lay out clear connected rooms with distinct hiding spots throughout the house interior.
agent_notes: Hide-and-seek is Party & Casual and the Childhood Game preset is the right build, but the answers make the house interior the entire play space, so I took interior-single from the shared catalogue instead of the preset's space-bounded — the whole map is one enclosed building with no exterior to generate, which also means no P3, since there is no outside-to-inside transition to link. Dropped the preset's obstacle-maze because the answers describe clear rooms and hiding spots rather than a warren whose topology is the challenge, and dropping it keeps the build off P6 honestly rather than by preference. cover-los carries the closets, furniture and clutter that make the hiding work, and social-hub is a room used for gathering between rounds at the stated 8-player size. With no stated round end I took the genre default that a round closes when the seeker tags the last hider, which is what trigger-scoring places.

notes: placement mirrored from option 'trigger-scoring': no siting rule given
